attacks.claim: TRAILING_PUNCT (/[.,;:!?)\]]+$/) is unanchored at the start and runs on every URL match. A URL containing a long run of punctuation followed by a non-punctuation character makes it backtrack quadratically. A neighbor-authored description of tens of thousands of dots can freeze the main thread for every viewer of that item page. The old code rendered plain text with no regex, and the artifact shows no length cap or input bound before tokenize.
attacks.evidence: const TRAILING_PUNCT = /[.,;:!?)\]]+$/; const raw = m[0].replace(TRAILING_PUNCT, ''); ABSENT: max description length or regex-time test

attacks.claim: A leading link is pushed whole even when it is far longer than the limit. A description that starts with a very long URL therefore stays uncollapsed, and the 'Show more' toggle then does nothing useful. This is a documented trade-off and the test encodes it, but it partly defeats the collapse goal.
attacks.evidence: else if (out.length === 0) out.push(t); // a leading link is shown whole rather than collapsing to nothing

attacks.claim: The code mixes UTF-16 code units (slice) with code points (Array.from) when cutting. The head slice can also split a surrogate pair at the limit.
attacks.evidence: Array.from(t.value).slice(0, limit).join('') vs t.value.slice(0, limit - used + 1)

attacks.claim: Unconditionally stripping a trailing ')' breaks balanced URLs such as Wikipedia-style paths ending in '(...)'.
The diff adds no overflow-wrap rule. A long unbroken URL link can overflow horizontally on narrow phone screens. Plain-text URLs already behaved this way, so this is not a regression.
Links open in a new tab with no announced or visible indication.
